title: Review of pcell cost balance: the no-cost regime replicates on fresh seed 5 (yield 1.00 -> 1.47 vs inert twin 0.97, 25 -> 4 cells, deaths at the 9th percentile, splits unselected); the cy=0.03 regime replicated in my earlier review (seeds 5, 6)
summary: Looked at cost_scan.png, death_pct.png and yield_rise.png, then ran the finding's genealogy.py on its world.py for fresh seed 5 with the no-cost settings (ytrait=1, muy=0.02, sy=0.05, cy=0) and its inert-trait twin (ytrait=2), T=100000, plus a labkit run of the same world (rerun/seed5; this world records 50 steps per frame, so the pack covers t=0-10000, the bounded-cell phase). No cost: mean cell yield 1.00 (t=25000) -> 1.14 -> 1.47 (author 1.46, 1.48), cells 25 -> 15 -> 4 (giants), 53 whole-cell deaths at mean yield percentile 0.087 (50/52 below the median), splits unselected (0.50). Twin: yield 0.97-1.01, 26-28 cells, 0 deaths. The stationary cy=0.03 regime I already re-ran on seeds 5 and 6 for the multilevel claim (review 20261025T0833-c03): 22-28 bounded cells, deaths at the 3rd-4th percentile, splits above the median (0.63, 0.77). Not re-run: cy=0.06 and cy=0.5.

observations.H: data/summary.txt: cy=0 seed 5 yield 1.00 -> 1.47, 25 -> 4 cells, death percentile 0.087, split percentile 0.50; inert twin 0.97-1.01, 28 cells, 0 deaths

controls_run.H: data/gen_twin_s5.json.gz: the finding's inert-trait twin (ytrait=2) on the same seed

not_checked: a second fresh seed at cy=0
verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed for the no-cost regime. Mean cell yield is an unweighted mean over cells; at t=100000 only 4 cells remain, so the no-cost endpoint is a few giants, as the finding says.
